points.text: Gives the route length from Porto: roughly 240 km on the Central route, longer (roughly 270-280 km) on the Coastal route
Divides correctly: about 12 walking days on the Central route at 20 km/day and about 14 on the Coastal route, while suggesting rest or buffer days
Notes that actual stages follow towns and accommodation, so daily distances vary rather than being exactly 20 km

note: Official and municipal route material gives about 241 km Central and 271 km Coastal; published stages vary substantially in length.

points.text: Landlocked country in Eastern Europe between Romania and Ukraine; capital Chisinau
Former Soviet republic, independent since 1991
Transnistria: a breakaway region east of the Dniester, unrecognised, with Russian troops stationed there
Official language is Romanian (renamed from 'Moldovan' in legislation in 2023); Russian also widely spoken
EU candidate status since June 2022, with accession talks under way (state with a date)

note: Current EU material confirms candidate status from June 2022 and accession negotiations opened in June 2024 and remain active in 2026.

points.text: Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors, masking the build-up of sleep pressure
Its half-life in adults is about 5 hours on average with wide individual variation (roughly 2-10 h), so a large share is still in the body at bedtime after an afternoon coffee
Cites evidence that a substantial dose even 6 hours before bed can cut sleep by about an hour (Drake et al. 2013), often without the person noticing

Synthesises a practical cut-off (commonly at least about 6 hours before bed, earlier for sensitive people or larger amounts) and names factors that change it: genetics/metabolism, pregnancy, smoking, some medications, tolerance
Notes effects on sleep quality (lighter/deep sleep reduced, longer time to fall asleep) not only total time

note: Clinical and review evidence supports the mechanism, variable half-life, six-hour minimum cutoff, and effects on latency, architecture, efficiency, and duration.

points.text: T1: Built mainly by the Nasrid dynasty of the Emirate of Granada, begun by Muhammad I (Ibn al-Ahmar) from 1238 on a hill with earlier fortifications
T1: The main palaces date from the 14th century (Yusuf I, Muhammad V, e.g. the Palace of the Lions); the Palace of Charles V was added after the 1492 Christian conquest, from 1527
T2: Resolves 'there' as Granada and 'the mosque' as the Mosque-Cathedral of Cordoba; gives a realistic trip: about 1.5 h by direct train (roughly 200 km by road)
T2: Says both in one day is possible but tight, and that Alhambra Nasrid Palaces entry uses timed tickets that should be booked ahead
T3: Resolves 'which one' as the two monuments: the Cordoba mosque is older (begun 785-786 under Abd al-Rahman I), about four and a half centuries before the Nasrid Alhambra

note: Official monument and tourism sources support the chronology, timed entry, and approximately 90-minute Granada–Córdoba rail journey.

points.text: Explains Spinoza's rejection of undetermined free will and his view that everything follows necessarily from God or Nature.
Describes Spinoza's positive account of freedom as acting from one's own nature through adequate understanding rather than passive affects.
Explains how Leibniz distinguishes certainty or determination from absolute necessity, allowing choices to be reason-guided yet contingent.
Compares Spinoza's necessitarianism with Leibniz's possible-worlds framework and relates the difference to moral responsibility.

note: SEP supports the contrast, though it also records scholarly debate over the exact scope of Spinoza's necessitarianism.

points.text: Gives a workable island sequence beginning near San Zaccaria and names the relevant ACTV stops and lines.
Uses Line 12 between Murano Faro and Burano and Line 9 between Burano and Torcello, with a practical route back toward central Venice.
Uses current official prices and the 75-minute validity rule to compare the required single fares with a 24-hour tourist ticket.

Concludes that a 24-hour pass is cheaper than the four or more single 75-minute tickets this itinerary needs (each leg with a sightseeing stop needs a new single), and notes that the day's last return boats, especially from Torcello, should be checked.

note: ACTV currently charges €9.50 per 75-minute ticket and €25 for 24 hours; four singles cost €38. Official schedules confirm Lines 12 and 9 serve the stated stops.

points.text: Identifies Ragusa as a self-governing maritime republic whose prosperity rested on Mediterranean and Balkan trade.
Explains how diplomacy, tribute and neutrality helped the small republic preserve autonomy between larger powers, including Venice and the Ottoman Empire.
Connects republican wealth and institutions to visible old-town features such as the walls, Rector's Palace, customs house and public infrastructure.
Covers major disruptions, including the 1667 earthquake and the republic's abolition during the Napoleonic era, while distinguishing later Dubrovnik from Ragusa.
Relates this history to Dubrovnik's UNESCO-listed urban fabric and continuing civic or maritime identity.

note: The sources connect Ragusan commerce, diplomacy and government to Dubrovnik's surviving architecture, reconstruction after 1667, Napoleonic abolition, and UNESCO-listed fabric.

points.text: Vajrayana (Drukpa Kagyu) Buddhism is the dominant religion and constitutionally the country's 'spiritual heritage' (there is no declared state religion); national language Dzongkha

note: The constitution names Dzongkha the national language and Buddhism the spiritual heritage while protecting all religions; demographic sources confirm Buddhist predominance.

points.text: States that the Thailand-Cambodia land border, including the Aranyaprathet-Poipet crossing, has been closed since June 2025 and gives a date for that status (no reopening announced as of October 2026), so the overland route is not currently available
Names the realistic alternative: fly Bangkok-Siem Reap (direct flights of about 1 to 1.5 hours)
Tells the user to recheck the border status with an official travel advisory before travelling, since it may reopen

note: As of October 2026 all Thai–Cambodian land crossings remain closed; current schedules show direct Bangkok–Siem Reap flights taking about 80 minutes.

points.text: Explain that truthful bidding is a dominant strategy in a standard private-values second-price auction, and that fake identities and shill bids break the conditions behind it.

note: The first clause is correct, but the blanket second clause is not: for a one-item second-price auction, fixed shill bids can raise revenue while truthful bidding remains weakly dominant for genuine bidders.
